title: Rabbah Zuti
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as Rav Ashi’s colleague who took a large part with him in arranging the Talmud, as in [Menachot 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.31b.2), where he tells Rav Ashi that Rabbi Yirmeyah of Difti transmitted the teaching in Rava’s name.

There, at [Menachot 52a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.52a.9), he said to Rav Ashi: “Come and hear.” In [Beitzah 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.32b.14) and [Bava Batra 120a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.120a.11) he said to Rav Ashi: “If so,” etc. In [Bekhorot 36a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.36a.11) he said to Ravina: “We teach it in the name of Rabbi Ila,” and there it reads Rava Zuti; Yuchasin’s reading is that he said it to Rav Nachman, and Hyman identifies him as the later Rav Nachman, son of Rav Huna.
He is mentioned in [Bava Kamma 108b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.108b.12) and [Zevachim 24a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.24a.7): “Rabbah Zuti asked it thus.”

In [Menachot 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.15b.9) it reads Rabbi Abba Zuti, but Hyman reports that the old printings and Shitah Mekubbetzet read Rabbah Zuti; Hyman identifies Abba with Rabbah or Rava.[^3]

notes.text: The role in arranging the Talmud, later Nachman identity and Abba/Rabbah/Rava equation remain Hyman’s claims. Distinct spelling and patronymics are preserved.

The consulted Menachot 31b directly has Rabbah Zuti speaking to Rav Ashi and reporting Yirmeyah of Difti in Rava’s name. It does not itself establish a role in arranging the Talmud, the later Nachman identification or the Abba/Rabbah/Rava equation. Those claims and exact old-print/Shitah/Yuchasin variants remain Hyman’s.

Menachot 31b has Rabbah Zuti tell Rav Ashi what Yirmeyah of Difti transmitted from Rava. The linked Bekhorot reads Rava Zuti, addressing Ravina. Menachot 15b has Rabbi Abba Zuti, one of the readings Hyman discusses. Heilprin also collects the Rabbah and Rava readings. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2740&lang=en).
